findings.text: Header offers allocation front ends for typed objects, counted objects, flexible trailing arrays, bucket selected sizes, node selected placement and caller tracked calls. Each front end adds default allocation flags, derives object type, forwards a size token and wraps the core with profiling hooks before reaching the node allocator.

When request size is known at compile time and nonzero, oversize requests divert to a large object path and the remainder select a cache by size index and allocation type. Non constant sizes use the generic node path with unchanged size and token.

Array allocation helpers for contiguous and virtually contiguous memory first compute element count product with overflow detection and return null on overflow without further action. Constant count and size combinations may use the inline node path, otherwise the generic node path is used.

Zeroing forms for slab caches, contiguous blocks, node placed blocks and virtually contiguous blocks behave as their non zeroing counterparts with the zero flag added. Counted zeroing forms combine overflow checked sizing with zeroing.

Virtually contiguous family provides alignment aware and node aware cores, default alignment of one, default node of no node, shorthand without node, and realloc forms that preserve alignment and node parameters while adding profiling hooks.
Hook invoked when scheduler is running for RCU deferred freeing performs no action in the routed configuration.

Swap setup flags use prefer indicator value hex 8000, priority mask hex 7fff, discard enable hex 10000, one time area discard hex 20000 and page cluster discard hex 40000. A valid mask is the union of all five values.

Swap entry type space reserves one marker type and conditionally reserves device, migration and poison counts of three, three and one when the corresponding features are enabled, else zero. Maximum usable swap files equals two raised to shift five minus all reserved counts.

When enabled, poison occupies the first index after usable files, migration read variants occupy the next three positions, device write read and exclusive occupy the following three, and the marker sits after all of them. Disabled builds collapse the corresponding counts to zero.

On disk swap header is a page sized union with two views. One view holds a large reserved area plus a ten byte magic signature. The other holds disk label space, version, last page, bad page count, two sixteen byte identifiers, padding and a trailing bad page list.

Reclaim accounting carries a counter for pages reclaimed outside LRU handling and optionally a pointer to per thread walk state under generational LRU. A helper adds a given count to the current task reclaim state when present.
Swap extent describes a contiguous mapping with a red black node for lookup, a start page offset, a length in pages and a start block on backing storage.

Swap device state flags mark used, writable, discard capable, discarding, solid state, block device, activated, area discard, page discard, stable writes, synchronous IO and hibernation pinning, using distinct single bit positions. Allocation cluster size is thirty two, with scaled skip and compaction limits derived from it, and an invalid entry is zero. Maximum tracked bad pages derives from header layout distance between bad page array and magic divided by integer size.
Number of tracked swap orders equals PMD order plus one when transparent huge page swap is available, otherwise one.

Per device sequential hint keeps a likely next allocation offset per order. Device descriptor keeps usage reference, state flags, priority, list links, type index, capacity, page totals, in use count, cluster metadata, free full nonfull fragmented and discard lists, global rotating cluster pointer, extent tree root, backing device and file, completion, work items, operations table and available list entry.

Global cluster use is serialized by a dedicated spin lock. A main device spin lock guards map scan related fields including in use counts and cluster lists, while remaining fields change only at activation or deactivation under a global swap lock. Flag changes need both locks with the global lock taken first.

A page to swap entry translation starts from the folio swap value and adds the page index within the folio. Free page count and swap cache totals are read from global zone and node statistics, and fullness compares remaining swap against half of total.
LRU cache drain progress moves through three ordered values representing not drained, drained for local context and drained everywhere.

LRU caching is considered disabled when a global disable counter is nonzero. Node reclaim registration is a no operation that reports success and unregistration does nothing in the routed configuration.
Global node statistic reads warn once when asked for a byte counted item, then return the atomic page count clamped at zero on multiprocessor builds to hide transient negative values.

Remaining swap pages and total swap pages are observed through atomic counters, with a helper reporting whether remaining pages are below half of total. Device reference release drops the per device usage reference.

When swap support is absent, device lookup returns null, reference release does nothing, page and swap totals report zero, swap full tests report false, swap info reports zero totals, folio and page release reduce to plain reference drops, entry duplication and reference counting report inert values, and extent addition fails with invalid argument.

Swap rate throttling and swap charge handling are bypassed when memory cgroup support is disabled, otherwise they delegate to internal helpers. Builds without cgroup swap report global swap counts and global fullness.
Managed zone iteration walks node zones between supplied indices and skips zones not under management, presenting only managed zones to the loop body.

Swap IO control overlays asynchronous control and block IO storage, plus a vector array sized to the cluster maximum with counts for vectors and length. A context pairs that control with its owning swap device. Operations table carries flags and callbacks for merge eligibility and for submitting reads and writes, with a flag marking file systems that require no filesystem reentry.

Memory pressure state tracks scanned and reclaimed counts with a spin lock keeping them consistent. First generation cgroup builds add tree accumulated counters, an event list with a mutex and a work item for deferred handling. Pressure severity uses ordered levels low, medium and critical plus a count sentinel.
Pressure scanned and reclaimed counters are kept mutually consistent under a dedicated spin lock, while pressure event list traversal and modification are guarded by a separate mutex.
In configurations without pressure notification, pressure reporting, priority adjustment and first generation initialization, cleanup and tree accounting are empty operations.

Reclaim statistics count dirty, unqueued dirty, congested, writeback, immediate, per anon file activations, reference retention, unmap failures, lazy free failures and demotions. Global dirty thresholds and page metadata counts are enumerated with a count sentinel, and per event counters are kept in a fixed array sized by event count.

Array sizing must fail closed on multiplication overflow before any allocation attempt. Callers must respect swap lock ordering and treat transient negative statistics as zero. Disabled swap, disabled cgroup and disabled LRU paths change helpers from accounting to no operation, so callers cannot rely on side effects there.
A predicate reports whether the current task is the swap reclaim daemon by testing a dedicated flag in task state.
Routed headers protect against multiple inclusion with conventional define guards for swap, swap operations, swap file, pressure and statistics headers.
